extracted.intended_audience: NIH SBIR/STTR applicants and principal investigators (grant applicants) and peer reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation and peer-review criteria for an NIH SBIR Phase I (R41) application, using the standard NIH review criteria (Significance, Investigators, Innovation, Approach, Environment) plus administrative review items (human/animal protections, biohazards, resource authentication, budget). Includes examples of strengths/weaknesses from reviewers and scoring/impact score calculation guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Assesses the importance of the problem being addressed and the potential for the proposed work to have a substantial impact. (Example criterion score reported: e.g., Significance: 2 / 1 / 1 across critiques.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer examples of strengths: new antifungals with new modes of action are desperately needed; occidiofungins have broad spectrum and potent antifungal activity including Candida and Cryptococcus; distinct structure relative to existing cyclic peptide antifungals; scientific premise is well justified by applicant publications. Reviewer examples of weaknesses: lack of knowledge regarding mechanism of action or lack of results with a purified compound makes analog generation a 'fishing expedition'; difficulty obtaining pure stereoisomers and production/separation problems could hamper development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluates whether the PD/PI, collaborators, and other researchers have the appropriate experience, training, and track record to carry out the proposed work. (Example criterion score reported: Investigator(s): 1 / 2 / 2 across critiques.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer examples of strengths: PI has led isolation and characterization of occidiofungins, documented in high-quality publications; PIs have filed patent(s); PIs have appropriate skills and some business experience (MBA). Reviewer examples of weaknesses: none stated in critiques, but reviewers note that additional preclinical/clinical development personnel will be needed as program progresses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Considers whether the project challenges and seeks to shift current research or clinical practice paradigms by using novel concepts, approaches, or methodologies. (Example criterion score: Innovation: 2 / 2 / 1 across critiques.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer examples of strengths: occidiofungins potentially represent an entirely new class of antifungal antibiotics; the compound has a novel mechanism distinct from current therapeutic targets; genetic system in producing strain demonstrated. Reviewer example of weakness: the screening proposed is routine (though needed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Assesses the strategy, methodology, and analyses proposed to accomplish the specific aims, including feasibility, potential problems, and alternative strategies. (Example criterion score: Approach: 4 / 2 / 3 across critiques.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer examples of strengths: multi-pronged approach combining biosynthetic (genetic inactivation) and synthetic chemistry to generate analogs; demonstrated utility of thioesterases to catalyze cyclization; logical plan to explore SAR and optimize fermentation. Reviewer examples of weaknesses: under-developed semisynthesis and solid-phase synthesis details, lack of discussion of occidiofungin yields from producing strain, genetic mutations may decrease yields, semisynthesis could produce mixtures if starting material is impure, unusual amino-acid precursors may complicate total synthesis, need for more detail about reaction conditions and target modifiers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Considers whether the scientific environment, institutional support, equipment, and available resources contribute to the probability of success. (Example criterion score: Environment: 1 / 2 / 4 across critiques.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer examples of strengths: facilities are excellent; environment appropriate for proposed work. Reviewer examples of weaknesses: as project progresses to IND preparation the company will need additional preclinical/clinical development personnel; a better description of certain institutional facilities (e.g., UT facilities) and production/scale-up plans would have helped.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact (Priority Score) and Scoring Procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: The overall impact reflects the reviewers' assessment of the likelihood for the project to exert a sustained, powerful influence on the research field(s) involved. Individual reviewers provide an overall impact score (1-9) and criterion scores (1-9) prior to the meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural notes from the summary: the impact/priority score is calculated after discussion by averaging the overall scores (1-9) given by all voting reviewers on the committee and multiplying by 10. Criterion scores are submitted prior to the meeting by the individual assigned reviewers, are not discussed specifically at the review meeting, and are not calculated into the overall impact score. Some applications also receive a percentile ranking. Reviewers' written critiques include strengths/weaknesses that inform the overall impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protections for Human Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Assesses whether the application appropriately addresses protections for human subjects when applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this application: Not Applicable (No Human Subjects). (When applicable, reviewers evaluate adequacy of protections; here the statement is explicit that no human subjects are involved.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluates the use of live vertebrate animals in the proposed research and the adequacy of proposed protections and justifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this application: Not Applicable (No live vertebrate animals involved for competing application). (When applicable, reviewers comment on appropriateness and welfare considerations.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Biohazards
rubrics_metrics.description: Assesses whether proposed activities involve biological agents, and whether appropriate biosafety plans are in place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this application: Not Applicable (No Biohazards). (When applicable, reviewers evaluate containment, training, and risk mitigation.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Review of plans to authenticate key biological and chemical resources (e.g., cell lines, reagents) to ensure reproducibility and validity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this application: Acceptable. Reviewers check whether authentication plans are adequate; here the SRO notes the assessment as 'Acceptable.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and Period of Support
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the proposed budget, period of support, potential overlaps with other funding, and recommended budget modifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee notes recommended budget modifications or identifies possible overlap (example: possible overlap with 1R41AI122441-01A1 for optimization of production and isolation). The ADMINISTRATIVE BUDGET NOTE warns requested budget has not been adjusted to reflect reviewer recommendations and that Institute grants management staff will calculate costs if an award is planned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee Budget Recommendations / Next Steps
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative recommendations regarding funding and instructions for next steps if the application is to be funded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example from this summary: 'The budget was recommended as requested.' SRG Action: Next Steps: Visit http://grants.nih.gov/grants/next_steps.htm. Institute grants management staff will calculate final costs based on committee recommendations. Footnote references NIH policies on resubmissions and links to peer review scoring details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Health Relevance (applicant-provided)
rubrics_metrics.description: Statement provided by applicant describing relevance of the proposed work to public health priorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example text in the application: proposal addresses need for development of novel broad spectrum antifungal for systemic infections; plans to isolate natural and produce semi-synthetic analogs to identify a lead compound for IND filing. While applicant-provided, reviewers consider public health relevance in judging significance and impact.
